result.journal: Transactions of the Institute of Measurement and Control
result.keywords: This paper presents an adaptive fuzzy hybrid framework that blends unscented filtering and robust H-infinity control concepts for simultaneous state estimation and stabilization of nonlinear systems. Two Takagi-Sugeno-Kang fuzzy inference modules are used to tune the combination weights between a hybrid unscented estimator and a robust disturbance-rejection component, allowing the method to respond to both Gaussian and non-Gaussian noise. A feedback-linearization layer is integrated with sliding-mode-inspired correction terms to improve performance on a fourth-order under-actuated inverted pendulum benchmark and a re-entry tracking scenario. The proposed adaptive fuzzy hybrid controller is evaluated against standard UKF, H-infinity, and hybrid baselines, showing improved tracking, bounded control effort, and reduced estimation error across multiple operating conditions.
result.title: Adaptive fuzzy hybrid controller for nonlinear state estimation and stabilization in under-actuated dynamics
